title: Which Direction Should Vinyl Plank Flooring Run?
meta: Which direction should vinyl plank run? Along the main sight line, toward the light, one way through the floor. Wills Flooring, Edmonds, $2.50 per sq ft.
keywords: which direction should vinyl plank flooring run, vinyl plank direction, lvp direction hallway, plank direction light source, vinyl plank layout open floor plan, Edmonds vinyl plank installation

blocks.lead: Run vinyl plank along the longest sight line from the main entry, which in most homes also means parallel to the longest wall and toward the biggest window. Then keep that one direction through the entire connected floor.
blocks.detail: Floating vinyl plank does not care about floor joists, so the decision is purely visual: sight line first, light second, room shape third. Wills Flooring installs vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft whatever the direction; only a diagonal changes the material waste.

blocks.html: Every Edmonds estimate ends with the same question at the front door: which way do the planks go? It matters more than people expect. The wrong direction makes a Seaview rambler feel shorter and choppier, and it cannot be fixed without pulling the floor. The good news: stand in the doorway you use most and the house usually tells you.

items.title: Follow the main sight line
items.text: Planks should run away from you as you walk in the front door, pulling the eye through the house. In an Edmonds rambler that is usually entry to living room to the view windows at the back. Length reads as space.

items.title: Run toward the light
items.text: Planks parallel to the light from the largest window hide the tiny shadows at every seam. Planks running across the light show every joint at 4 p.m. Bowl and Seaview homes with big west windows toward the Sound feel this most.

items.title: Long dimension of the room
items.text: Running with the long wall makes a room feel longer and cuts the number of end joints. Running across a narrow hall makes it a ladder. When rules 1 and 2 disagree, the long dimension of the main room breaks the tie.

items.title: One direction, whole floor
items.text: Open-plan main floors get one direction from front door to back slider, kitchen included. Every change of direction needs a T-molding, and every T-molding is a line that chops the space.

blocks.html: Direction does not change our labor rate. A 950 sq ft Westgate main floor is 950 × $2.50 = $2,375 for vinyl plank installation, with plank, underlayment and old-floor removal quoted separately. A diagonal layout adds material waste, not labor cost, and the calculator below handles stairs at $100 each.

blocks.note: Straight layouts need about 7 to 10 percent extra plank for cuts. Diagonal or herringbone layouts need 15 percent or more; we size the order at the estimate.

items.text: End joints in neighboring rows should be offset at least 6 to 8 in, and never repeat every other row. A regular step pattern or an H pattern reads as a mistake from across the room.
We measure the room so the last row is at least half a plank wide. A sliver against the far wall is the most common sign of an unplanned start.
Straight runs use about 7 to 10 percent extra. Diagonal layouts need 15 to 20 percent because every wall cut is a triangle. Order to the layout, not the square footage.
items.note: Extra plank left over is worth keeping for future repairs.

items.text: Most rigid-core plank allows continuous runs of 40 to 60 ft before a T-molding is required. Edmonds ramblers rarely hit that; long townhouse rows can.

blocks.text: When to change direction, and when not to

a.title: Reasonable when
items: A closed door separates a long narrow room from the hall and it would look like a ladder otherwise
The manufacturer's run length is exceeded and a T-molding is going in anyway
A different level of a split-level starts at a landing
You are deliberately framing a kitchen with a border or a diagonal field

b.title: Do not change when
items: The rooms are open to each other with no door
The only reason is that each room is longer the other way
The change would put a T-molding in the middle of a walking path
It is the installer's preference for fewer cuts rather than your sight line

blocks.title: About diagonal:
blocks.text: Planks at 45 degrees can make a small square room feel bigger and hide walls that are out of square, which is common in 1950s Edmonds houses. But it costs more plank, shows every wall cut, and dates faster than a straight run. We suggest it rarely, and only in a single room.
Direction mistakes we get called to fix

items.html: Following the joists. An old rule for nailed hardwood. Floating vinyl plank never touches the joists. Installers who insist on it are quoting a hardwood habit.
Optimizing each room separately. Four rooms, three directions and three T-moldings in a 1,000 sq ft house. The floor looks patched before it is a week old.
Starting against the wrong wall. Starting on a crooked wall means the crookedness runs across the whole floor. We snap a straight line off the longest straight wall and cut the first row to it.

Ignoring the afternoon light. A floor that looks fine at 10 a.m. shows every seam when the sun drops over the Sound. We check the plank direction against the biggest window before the first row locks in.

items: Stand in the front door and note the longest sight line; that is your default direction
Note where the biggest window is, and whether it is west-facing toward the water
Walk every hallway and confirm the planks will run lengthwise down it
List every doorway where a direction change is tempting and decide on each one before ordering
Confirm the plank order includes waste for the layout you chose, not just the area
Ask the installer which wall they will start from and why
If a room seems to need a diagonal, get a mock-up of five loose planks on the floor first

faq.q: Should vinyl plank run the same direction in every room?
faq.a: Yes, wherever rooms are open to each other. One direction through the whole connected floor makes the house feel bigger and avoids T-moldings in walking paths. The exception is a closed room that is long and narrow the other way, where breaking at the door is acceptable.

faq.q: Should planks run parallel or perpendicular to the front door?
faq.a: Away from the front door, so they run perpendicular to the door itself and parallel to your line of sight as you walk in. That pulls the eye through the house. In most Edmonds ramblers this also points the planks at the living room windows.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank need to run perpendicular to floor joists?
faq.a: No. That rule is for nailed solid hardwood, which needs the joists for fastening. Floating vinyl plank sits on the subfloor and never touches the joists, so direction is chosen for looks alone. Over a flat plywood subfloor, any direction is structurally fine.

faq.q: Which way should vinyl plank run in a hallway?
faq.a: Lengthwise, down the length of the hall. Planks running across a 36 or 42 in hallway create a joint every plank width and make the hall feel like a ladder. Lengthwise runs read as one long runway and use fewer cuts.

faq.q: Is diagonal vinyl plank a good idea?
faq.a: Occasionally, in one square room where walls are out of square or you want a small space to feel larger. It needs 15 to 20 percent more plank, shows every wall cut, and tends to date. Wills Flooring charges the same $2.50 per sq ft labor either way; the extra cost is material.

faq.q: Can the direction be changed after the floor is installed?
faq.a: Only by taking the floor up. Click-lock plank can be unlocked and relaid, but cut planks at the walls rarely fit the new direction, so expect to buy 20 to 30 percent new material. It is far cheaper to lay five loose planks and decide before installation.
